routes.description: Establish a cumulative theistic explanation from cosmic origin and order, biological information, rational consciousness, objective morality, scientific regularity, and historically grounded religious claims.
routes.successCriteria: Show that these features jointly require or are better accounted for by an immaterial, intelligent, personal, and morally authoritative creator, while answering naturalistic alternatives and the principal objections from evil and religious uncertainty.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative case to the conclusion that theism explains the disputed features of reality more adequately than skeptical naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Derive a transcendent and causally adequate ground from the beginning, contingency, and ordered conditions of material reality.
Establish that biological information and nature's lawlike, goal-directed order require an intelligent source beyond unguided physical processes.
Establish that trustworthy rational thought and meaningful agency require grounding in a rational mind rather than wholly determined material reactions.
Establish that objective moral value, evil, and ultimate justice require a standard grounded beyond human attitudes and social development.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve the theistic inference by answering objections from suffering, apparent imperfection, cosmic timing, and competing natural histories.
Supply publicly relevant historical grounds for moving from generic theism toward Christianity through the resurrection claim.

routes.description: Defend skeptical naturalism through evidential restraint, scientific explanation, emergent accounts of mind and morality, and objections to the explanatory sufficiency and expected consequences of theism.
routes.successCriteria: Show that theistic conclusions outrun the available evidence, that naturalistic mechanisms or open inquiry address the disputed phenomena without divine agency, and that suffering, imperfection, religious diversity, and weak miracle evidence reduce theism's comparative adequacy.

motionBridge.description: Connect scientific inquiry and evidential restraint to the conclusion that skeptical naturalism is the better-supported approach to explaining reality.

centralBridges.description: Require publicly assessable evidence, possible disconfirmation, and explanatory mechanisms before accepting supernatural causal claims.
Provide naturalistic accounts of biological development, rational agency, morality, purpose, and improbable events without invoking divine agency.
Show that cosmic origins and unresolved explanatory gaps do not uniquely establish a finite beginning, a transcendent cause, or the Christian God.
Show that suffering, apparent imperfection, cosmic timing, and religious nonconvergence conflict with expectations generated by the proposed God.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Contrast science's organized error correction and convergence with faith-based methods and incompatible religious conclusions.
Apply evidential, probabilistic, and selection-bias considerations to resurrection, miracle, and providence claims.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin, Contingency, and Order
sections.rationale: Covers whether the universe's beginning, material composition, initial conditions, and regularity require a transcendent intelligent cause or remain open to natural histories and competing possibilities.

sections.title: Biological Information and Evolutionary Explanation
sections.rationale: Addresses whether genetic information and the first replicating system indicate intelligent agency or whether evolutionary mechanisms and physical conditions adequately explain biological complexity.

sections.title: Reason, Consciousness, and Agency
sections.rationale: Tests whether material naturalism can ground trustworthy reasoning and volition or whether these capacities require a rational, nonmaterial source.

sections.title: Morality, Evil, and Justice
sections.rationale: Encompasses the dispute over objective moral grounding, secular accounts based on harm and reciprocity, the evidential problem of suffering, and claims about ultimate justice.

sections.title: Evidence, Science, and Explanatory Method
sections.rationale: Examines burdens of belief, falsifiability, explanatory gaps, scientific correction, and whether invoking God supplies an adequate causal explanation of reality.

sections.title: Religious Diversity and Resurrection Evidence
sections.rationale: Addresses whether incompatible religions and personal faith undermine specific Christian claims or whether cumulative and historical resurrection evidence distinguishes Christianity.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: The universe's beginning and precise initial conditions are better explained by a powerful, intelligent, spaceless, timeless, and immaterial creator than by chance.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Materialism undermines confidence in rational belief because physically determined mental activity would be reaction rather than truth-directed reasoning, whereas theism grounds reason in a rational mind.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: The specified information in DNA is positive evidence of an intelligent source because messages and programs are known to originate from minds rather than blind natural laws.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Objective moral comparisons require a standard beyond humanity, and that external, unchanging moral standard is grounded in God's nature.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: The recognition of evil and injustice presupposes objective goodness and justice, which ultimately require God rather than disprove God's existence.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: The reliable order, lawlike regularity, and goal-directed behavior required by science point to an external intellect that creates and sustains nature.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: Materially composed reality requires an external composer that cannot itself be composed, yielding one immaterial, spaceless, timeless being of pure actuality.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: Christianity is supported by a cumulative case for truth, God, miracles, reliable resurrection testimony, and Jesus's divine authority.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: Evolutionary replication does not explain the prior origin of the genetic code and the system capable of replication.

chunk-004:c004-10.proposition: Christianity rests on the historical resurrection event rather than merely biblical assertion, with the disciples' costly testimony offered as evidence.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: A defensible atheistic stance withholds belief in God until sufficient evidence appears rather than asserting certainty that no God exists.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Saying that an omnipotent, omniscient, benevolent God caused a phenomenon does not identify how it occurred and therefore does not itself supply a causal mechanism.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Science and reason are methods people practice, and using those methods to argue that they cannot stand without theism is self-undermining.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Preventable childhood suffering has scientifically identifiable causes and remedies but is difficult to reconcile with an all-knowing, all-powerful, wholly good God.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: Rational agency and degrees of volition can emerge at higher explanatory levels even when organisms are materially constituted and physically constrained.

chunk-003:c003-04.proposition: An indefinitely old succession of universes remains a possible natural history, so the present universe does not logically require a finite first beginning.

chunk-003:c003-05.proposition: The immense interval before humanity and Christianity makes a human-centered, purposive divine plan appear implausibly and inefficiently timed.

chunk-003:c003-07.proposition: Persistent religious diversity without evidential convergence undermines confidence in Christianity's exclusive truth, unlike scientific disputes that tend toward evidence-driven consensus.

chunk-003:c003-09.proposition: The second law of thermodynamics does not preclude evolution because Earth is an open system receiving energy that can drive local increases in biological complexity.

chunk-004:c004-02.proposition: Objective morality can develop from social instincts, reciprocal perspective-taking, upbringing, and cultural moral progress without divine grounding.

chunk-004:c004-05.proposition: Apparently miraculous and extremely improbable personal outcomes are expected across many opportunities and are exaggerated by hindsight and selection bias.
